qa.a: That's a good question because I don't know many people who would be considered to be that way. And they might feel superior to other people if they're doing really well but other people aren't doing as well.

qa.q: Do you think artists with talents should focus on their talents only?
qa.a: If you mean focus on their talents to the detriment of everything else then no, it's probably not such a good idea.

qa.q: If you're only good at one narrow thing and don't develop skills in other areas then it's going to be a rather dull life, isn't it?
qa.a: Moreover, if your talent or work opportunities in your area of expertise dry up, it's better to have a key skill and then some backups on hand just in case.

qa.q: And how can they develop their key skills?
qa.a: Well by practicing, that's how you develop anything.

qa.q: Is it possible for us to know whether young children will become musicians or painters when they grow up?
qa.a: They might just place some sort of natural aptitude for art before they even hit adulthood. Or they could even just express an interest in those areas but it's probably not a good idea to pigeonhole children and label them before they're ready.

qa.q: Do you think that the government should support these children or like genius children?
qa.a: Well, it will depend on the individual country and if they have the resources available but let's assume that they do then yes and probably their education system, if it's functioning correctly, should do that, should be flexible enough to allow them to flourish while other people are doing the baseline.

qa.q: Why do people like to watch anything?
qa.a: It's the novelty of the experience I suppose. You can see people doing things that you've never seen before or at the very least you've never tried yourself and you can sort of live vicariously through them.

qa.q: And do you think talent shows are popular in general?
qa.a: Well if viewing figures are anything to go by then yes and the newspaper coverage seems to indicate that it's quite popular.

qa.q: It will be even more popular in the future?
qa.a: Well I don't know how they would be different because there are always different talents. Maybe the format might change, maybe audience participation. Anyway, I don't know if different ones will be popular but certainly the concept of talent shows will be popular.

qa.q: Do you think it's more interesting to watch famous people or ordinary people's shows?
qa.a: I think it depends on what you want to focus on. Shows about famous people tend to focus on big events and drama and major issues while ordinary people have their own quieter personal dramas which are more relatable to draw people's focus.

qa.q: Why they like it or why they dislike it?
qa.a: Dislike them. Well I imagine because it seems a more productive use of time to develop your own talents rather than looking at other people. Well rather than looking at other people developing theirs. So yes, in this perspective it seems better for them to work on themselves.

qa.q: Some people say that you are born with a certain talent so would you agree?
qa.a: Well you may be born with a natural inclination in that direction but talent will come about through practice and if they don't use it then it will just remain an inclination to do something.
